items.title: The people who run bookings and beds are missing from the evidence
items.whyItMatters: Both retrieved records studied clinicians and women; the booking process that creates the mismatch (claim c1) is run by clerks and bed managers.
items.opportunity: Include booking clerks, bed managers and labour ward coordinators in the sample.

items.title: Women with the worst experiences may not be reached
items.whyItMatters: Recruiting through the unit may miss women who were upset, do not speak English or had a poor outcome.
items.opportunity: Recruit through community midwives and the maternity voices group, offer interpreters, and sample for ethnicity, parity and language.

items.title: Evidence was thin after the first search failed
items.whyItMatters: Only two records were retrieved; five leads remain unchecked.
items.opportunity: Retrieve and check the leads on capacity-linked booking before recommendations cite them.

items.title: Themes alone will not guide redesign
items.whyItMatters: The unit manager wants practical recommendations.
items.opportunity: Map themes to the steps of the booking and start process in a framework matrix.

reevaluation: The gaps support a qualitative study across the whole booking chain with deliberate sampling of women who are hard to reach.
summary: Four gaps: missing booking staff, hard-to-reach women, thin evidence and the need for actionable output.
